cards.explanation: The answer is to return to the LORD and obey His voice. Moses, Israel's leader, says they and their children “…return to the LORD your God and obey His voice with all your heart and all your soul…” So the kids are in on it too. That's a whole family turning around together, like a car full of people finally agreeing to pull over and ask for directions.

The answer is that the LORD will gather them from all the nations. Moses says the LORD “…will restore you from captivity and have compassion on you and gather you from all the nations…” Compassion is right there in the middle of it. I love how personal that is, friends, because He is the One doing the gathering.

The answer is False. Moses says the LORD “…will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will take possession of it.” And then it gets better: “He will cause you to prosper and multiply more than your fathers.” (Deuteronomy 30:5) Less? No, no, no, that's MORE, friends, and I'd take a bigger batch over a smaller one any day of the week.

The answer is that they will love Him with all their heart and soul. Moses says the LORD “…will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, and you will love Him with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.” Notice who does the circumcising: the LORD. The love is what Moses says the people will do after that. And it ends with “…so that you may live.”

The answer is on the enemies who hate and persecute them. Moses says, “Then the LORD your God will put all these curses upon your enemies who hate you and persecute you.” So the curses end up on the ones who hate and persecute them. Quite a turn of events.

The answer is delight. Moses says, “…the LORD will again delight in your prosperity, as He delighted in that of your fathers…” The word "again" matters, because it's something that happened before. A word like delight tells you how the LORD feels about His people.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD will make them abound “…if you obey the LORD your God by keeping His commandments and statutes that are written in this Book of the Law, and if you turn to Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” Both pieces go together, friends: what's written and a heart turned toward Him. A recipe card doesn't help much if you never turn on the oven.

The answer is False. Moses says, “For this commandment I give you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach.” It's within their grasp. I wish every instruction manual I've ever met could say that.

The answer is in their mouth and in their heart. Moses says, “But the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it.” Nobody has to climb or sail anywhere to get it. It's already close enough to say out loud and carry inside.

The answer is to love the LORD and walk in His ways. Moses says, “For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances…” Love the LORD, walk in His ways, keep His commandments. That's the command in Moses' own words.

The answer is True. Moses says, “For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, and to keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances, so that you may live and increase…” Living and increasing are the goal he states. He also says the LORD may bless them in the land they're entering to possess.

The answer is that they will surely perish. Moses declares, “…you will surely perish; you shall not prolong your days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.” It comes after he describes a heart that turns away and bows down to other gods. It's a heavy line, friends, and I think it hits hard.

The answer is heaven and earth. Moses says, “I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing.” That's about as big a witness stand as you could ask for. And it all leads into his next words: “Therefore choose life…”

The answer is they and their descendants. Moses says, “Therefore choose life, so that you and your descendants may live…” The choice reaches past the people in front of him to the generations after them. A fresh batch of dough today turns into cookies someone else gets to enjoy.

The answer is their life. Moses says, “For He is your life…” That's the reason behind loving the LORD, obeying Him and holding fast to Him. I think that's one of the sweetest lines in the whole sermon, friends.
